cohort: The study included 116 symptomatic and asymptomatic women aged 18-45 years who had undergone one or more cesarean sections.
finding: Repeated cesarean deliveries significantly increase both the risk and severity of isthmocele, with its prevalence rising to 100% after the fourth cesarean, and a niche length of >= 5 mm proving to be the most reliable morphometric marker for symptomatic cases.
mod_finding: Repeated cesarean deliveries (a mode of birth) significantly increase both the risk and severity of isthmocele formation.
